out.other_title: Less human feedback makes it easier to deploy models not tested or observed by humans
out.rationale: Bai et al. state that reducing human feedback makes it easier to deploy models not tested by humans, with unforeseen failure modes. Goel et al. report more capable LMs make more similar mistakes and argue that as humans defer more to AI oversight, correlated failures pose safety risks; the argument extrapolates a capability-similarity trend measured on MCQ benchmarks.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether replacing human feedback with AI oversight introduces new failure risks, for LLM judges and training on LM annotations

open_obligations: Check whether samples from one model have correlated errors that violate Choi et al.'s independence assumption.
Note that Goel et al.'s similarity is across different models, not repeated samples.
Check Choi et al.'s condition that the correct answer is the most probable option.
out.other_title: Majority voting success probability approaches 1 as the number of agents grows
out.rationale: Choi, Zhu and Li prove majority voting succeeds with probability approaching 1 as N grows, assuming homogeneous independent agents whose top belief is on the correct answer. Goel et al. report more capable models make more similar mistakes and argue this weakens LM juries through compromised independence; Goel et al. measure similarity across models from different developers, while Choi et al.'s agents are samples from one model, so the challenge is to the independence assumption in practice.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether adding more LLM voters reliably drives majority-vote accuracy toward 1

text: The authors argue that if the trend continues it could mean greater affinity bias in LM judges, lower gains from inter-LM training, and weaker benefits from LM juries through compromised independence and amplified collective biases; most concerningly, they say their results indicate that as model blind spots get harder to detect and humans defer more to AI oversight, models also make more similar mistakes, posing safety risks from correlated failures.
title: Correlated failures risk: deferring to AI oversight as model blind spots converge
